```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(finalfit)
library(oncreportr)

analysis_data <- read.csv(
  "../data/processed/data.csv",
  na.strings = "",
  check.names = FALSE
)

key_variables <- c("iso", "year")
analysis_variables <- setdiff(names(analysis_data), key_variables)
outcome_variables <- intersect(c("matmor", "infmor", "neomor", "un5mor"),
                               names(analysis_data))

# Single source of display labels for every dataset column.
recode <- tibble(
  var = c(
    "iso", "year", "matmor", "infmor", "neomor", "un5mor", "gdp_1000",
    "oecd", "pop_dens", "urban", "age_dep", "male_edu", "temp",
    "rainfall_1000", "Drought", "Earthquake", "death_sum", "conflict",
    "conflict_intensity", "death_sum_quintile", "any_missingness"
  ),
  label = c(
    "Country (ISO code)", "Year", "Maternal mortality", "Infant mortality",
    "Neonatal mortality", "Under-5 mortality", "GDP per capita", "OECD member",
    "Population density", "Urban residence", "Age dependency ratio",
    "Male education", "Temperature", "Rainfall", "Drought", "Earthquake",
    "Battle-related deaths", "Armed conflict", "Conflict intensity",
    "Battle-related deaths: none or positive-death quintile", "Any Missingness"
  )
)
stopifnot(all(names(analysis_data) %in% recode$var))

variable_labels <- setNames(recode$label, recode$var)
label_variable <- function(x) {
  labels <- unname(variable_labels[as.character(x)])
  ifelse(is.na(labels), as.character(x), labels)
}

# Use compact, centred tables that stay within the page width in PDF output.
format_table <- function(x, ..., font_size = 8) {
  table <- kableExtra::kbl(x, ..., booktabs = TRUE)

  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    table |>
      kableExtra::kable_styling(
        latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position", "scale_down"),
        font_size = font_size,
        full_width = FALSE,
        position = "center"
      )
  } else {
    table |>
      kableExtra::kable_styling(
        bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed", "responsive"),
        full_width = FALSE,
        position = "center"
      )
  }
}
```

## First look at the data

```{r}
#| label: variable-classes

# Keep the country code as a character identifier; use numeric types for
# continuous measures and factors for binary indicators.
continuous_variables <- intersect(
  c(
    "matmor", "infmor", "neomor", "un5mor", "gdp_1000", "pop_dens",
    "urban", "age_dep", "male_edu", "temp", "rainfall_1000", "death_sum"
  ),
  names(analysis_data)
)
binary_variables <- intersect(
  c("oecd", "Drought", "Earthquake", "conflict"),
  names(analysis_data)
)

analysis_data <- analysis_data |>
  mutate(
    iso = as.character(iso),
    year = as.integer(year),
    across(all_of(continuous_variables), as.numeric),
    across(all_of(binary_variables), ~ factor(.x, levels = c(0, 1)))
  )

make_death_quintile <- function(x) {
  result <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  result[!is.na(x) & x == 0] <- "None (0 deaths)"

  positive_deaths <- !is.na(x) & x > 0
  result[positive_deaths] <- paste0(
    "Positive deaths: quintile ",
    dplyr::ntile(x[positive_deaths], n = 5)
  )

  factor(
    result,
    levels = c(
      "None (0 deaths)",
      paste0("Positive deaths: quintile ", 1:5)
    ),
    ordered = TRUE
  )
}

analysis_data <- analysis_data |>
  mutate(
    conflict_intensity = factor(
      case_when(
        is.na(death_sum) ~ NA_character_,
        death_sum < 25 ~ "No conflict (<25 deaths)",
        death_sum < 1000 ~ "Minor conflict (25-999 deaths)",
        death_sum >= 1000 ~ "War (>=1,000 deaths)"
      ),
      levels = c(
        "No conflict (<25 deaths)",
        "Minor conflict (25-999 deaths)",
        "War (>=1,000 deaths)"
      ),
      ordered = TRUE
    ),
    death_sum_quintile = make_death_quintile(death_sum)
  )

# Include the derived conflict measures in the downstream summaries and plots.
analysis_variables <- setdiff(names(analysis_data), key_variables)

variable_classes <- tibble(
  Variable = label_variable(names(analysis_data)),
  Class = vapply(analysis_data, function(x) class(x)[1], character(1))
)
format_table(variable_classes)

analysis_data <- analysis_data |>
  mutate(
    any_missingness = if_any(all_of(analysis_variables), is.na)
  )

```


```{r}
#| label: data-sample

set.seed(20261026)
sample_columns <- intersect(
  c(key_variables, outcome_variables, "gdp_1000", "rainfall_1000", "male_edu", "conflict"),
  names(analysis_data)
)
sample_data <- analysis_data |>
  slice_sample(n = min(10, nrow(analysis_data))) |>
  select(all_of(sample_columns))
format_table(sample_data, col.names = label_variable(names(sample_data)))

```

## Individual variables

The table below gives the type, observed range, and overall missingness of each analysis variable. 

```{r}
#| label: variable-summary

variable_summary <- analysis_data |>
  summarise(across(
    all_of(analysis_variables),
    list(
      class = ~ class(.x)[1],
      missing_n = ~ sum(is.na(.x)),
      missing_prop = ~ mean(is.na(.x)),
      minimum = ~ if (!is.numeric(.x) || all(is.na(.x))) NA_real_ else min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      median = ~ if (!is.numeric(.x) || all(is.na(.x))) NA_real_ else median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      maximum = ~ if (!is.numeric(.x) || all(is.na(.x))) NA_real_ else max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}__{.fn}"
  )) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
    names_sep = "__"
  ) |>
  mutate(variable = label_variable(variable)) |>
  arrange(desc(missing_prop), variable)

format_table(
  variable_summary,
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Variable", "Class", "Missing (n)", "Missing (%)", "Minimum", "Median", "Maximum")
)


```

# visualizing year pattern in missing maternal mortality data
```{r}
analysis_data  |> group_by(`Missing Maternal Mortality` =  is.na(matmor), year)  |> tally()
```

There's >1% missingness in two variables. Maternal mortality is missing in 11.5% of observations, as it is only observed from 2000-2017. GPD per capita is missing in 1.7% of observations. 



```{r}
#| label: outcome-distributions
#| fig-cap: "Distributions of mortality outcomes across country-years."

analysis_data |>
  pivot_longer(
    all_of(outcome_variables),
    names_to = "outcome",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, colour = "white", fill = "#2C7FB8") +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free", labeller = as_labeller(variable_labels)) +
  labs(x = "Mortality rate", y = "Country-years", title = "Mortality outcome distributions") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Missing data

The following plots show whether missingness is patterned by time, country, or conflict status. 


```{r}
#| label: missingness-data
#| include: false

missing_long <- analysis_data |>
  mutate(
    conflict_status = case_when(
      is.na(conflict) ~ "Conflict status missing",
      as.character(conflict) == "0" ~ "No conflict",
      as.character(conflict) == "1" ~ "Conflict",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    conflict_status = factor(
      conflict_status,
      levels = c("No conflict", "Conflict", "Conflict status missing", "Other")
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    all_of(analysis_variables),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value",
    values_transform = list(value = as.character)
  ) |>
  mutate(is_missing = is.na(value))

missing_by_year <- missing_long |>
  group_by(year, variable) |>
  summarise(proportion_missing = mean(is_missing), .groups = "drop")

missing_by_country <- missing_long |>
  group_by(iso, variable) |>
  summarise(proportion_missing = mean(is_missing), .groups = "drop")

missing_by_conflict <- missing_long |>
  group_by(conflict_status, variable) |>
  summarise(proportion_missing = mean(is_missing), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
#| label: missingness-by-year
#| fig-cap: "Proportion missing for each variable in each year."

ggplot(missing_by_year,
       aes(x = year, y = variable, fill = proportion_missing)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = label_variable) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Variable", fill = "Missing", title = "Missingness by year") +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
#| label: missingness-by-country
#| fig-cap: "Proportion missing for each variable within each country over 2000--2019."

ggplot(missing_by_country,
       aes(x = iso, y = variable, fill = proportion_missing)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = label_variable) +
  labs(x = "Country (ISO code)", y = "Variable", fill = "Missing",
       title = "Missingness by country") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
```


## viewing some data where variables are missing

```{r}
#| label: missingvars
sample_data <- analysis_data |> 
  filter(is.na(infmor)) |> 
  select(all_of(sample_columns))
format_table(sample_data, col.names = label_variable(names(sample_data)))

sample_data <- analysis_data |> 
  filter(is.na(rainfall_1000)) |> 
  select(all_of(sample_columns))
format_table(sample_data, col.names = label_variable(names(sample_data)))

```

As shown in @missingness-by-country, some countries may have missing data in multiple variables. For example Puerto Rico with mortality outcomes data,  Ivory Coast in weather and education variables. 

```{r}
#| label: missingness-by-conflict
#| fig-cap: "Proportion missing for each variable by conflict status."


ggplot(missing_by_conflict,
       aes(x = conflict_status, y = variable, fill = proportion_missing)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = label_variable) +
  labs(x = "Armed conflict status", y = "Variable", fill = "Missing",
       title = "Missingness by conflict status") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: missingness-by-conflict-table

missingtab <- analysis_data |> 
  group_by(conflict, any_missingness) |> 
  tally() |> 
  group_by(conflict) |> 
  mutate(
proportion_missing = n/sum(n)
)
format_table(missingtab) 
```

Missingness is slightly higher in country-years with armed conflict. There are 3205 observations with no missingness in any variables. 

## Relationship between conflict and mortality outcomes

This descriptive plot compares mortality outcomes across the observed conflict
indicator. It is not an adjusted or causal comparison.

```{r}
#| label: outcomes-by-conflict
#| fig-cap: "Mortality outcomes by conflict status."

analysis_data |>
  filter(!is.na(conflict)) |>
  mutate(
    conflict_status = if_else(
      as.character(conflict) == "1", "Conflict", "No conflict"
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    all_of(outcome_variables),
    names_to = "outcome",
    values_to = "mortality_rate"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = conflict_status, y = mortality_rate, fill = conflict_status)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.25, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free_y", labeller = as_labeller(variable_labels)) +
  labs(x = "Armed conflict status", y = "Mortality rate",
       title = "Mortality outcomes by conflict status") +
  theme_minimal()
```

##  Descriptive summary table of all variables in dataset by binary armed conflict status 
- all continuous variables summarized by median and IQR
```{r}
#| label: data-overview

byvar <- "conflict"
vars <- setdiff(analysis_variables, byvar)

conflict_summary <- function(continuous_summary) {
  finalfit::summary_factorlist(
    analysis_data,
    dependent = byvar,
    explanatory = vars,
    na_include = TRUE,
    na_to_prop = F, 
    cont = continuous_summary,
    add_col_totals = TRUE, 
    add_row_totals = TRUE,
    total_col = TRUE
  ) |>
    mutate(label = label_variable(label)) |>
    rename(
      Variable = label,
      `Level or summary` = levels,
      `No conflict` = `0`,
      `Armed conflict` = `1`,
    )
}

conflict_summary("median") |> format_table(digits = 2)
```

##  Descriptive summary table of all variables in dataset by binary armed conflict status 
- all continuous variables summarized by mean and sd
```{r}
vars <- continuous_variables
conflict_summary("mean") |> format_table(digits = 2)
```
